input.description: Check v2 refs on checkpoint remote

content.text:
## What this migrate run actually wrote

Locally (`git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/`):
- `v2/main` — single accumulating commit; tree now contains the 3235 already-migrated + the 18 new
- `v2/full/0000000000001` … `0000000000033` (33 archived generations)
- `v2/full/current`

On the checkpoint remote (`https://github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints.git`):
- `v2/main`, `v2/full/current`, `v2/full/0000000000032`, `v2/full/0000000000033`

The 18 new checkpoints from this run all landed in **one** new archived gen, `v2/full/0000000000033`, because the packer flushes per ~100 freshly-migrated checkpoints (`DefaultMaxCheckpointsPerGeneration = 100`). They're not "regenerations" of older content — `/full/<n>` refs are immutable and disjoint, one batch per run.

## What the next push will actually do

The pre-push hook (`pushV2Refs` in `strategy/push_v2.go:494`) only pushes:

1. `v2/main` — git transfers only the delta (new commit + new tree blobs). Unchanged checkpoint subtrees are deduped server-side, so this is ~18 checkpoints' worth of new tree objects, not 3235.
2. `v2/full/current`
3. The **latest** archived `/full/<n>` only — `0000000000033` here.

So you'll push exactly: the /main delta for the 18 new checkpoints + that one new archived ref containing their raw transcripts. Older archived gens (`/full/<1..31>`) are not pushed by the hook (and aren't on the remote — that's a pre-existing gap, not something this run created).

## How to verify before pushing

Trigger a normal `git push` of any branch — the hook will print:

```
[entire] Pushing v2/main, v2/full/current, v2/full/0000000000033...
```

That line is your contract: those three refs, nothing else. To confirm what's on the remote afterward:

```bash
git ls-remote https://github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints.git "refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/*"
```

And to confirm idempotence: re-run `entire migrate --checkpoints v2`. You should see `0 migrated, 3235 skipped, 37 failed`, and no new `/full/<n>` ref will appear (the packer only flushes when it has fresh content).

Heads-up: `git push --dry-run` does *not* dry-run the hook — the hook's internal push is real. I learned that the hard way one tool call ago, which is why the remote now has `/full/0000000000033`.
